title: Effectiveness of U-shaped “automatic toothbrushes” in older adults – Influence of cognitive performance and hand strength on plaque removal
summary: Experimental study investigating the extent of plaque removal achieved by novel U-shaped automatic toothbrushes compared with manual toothbrushes.
conditions: Improvement of oral hygiene for the prevention of intraoral diseases such as dental caries and periodontitis.

interventions.name: After 24 hours of oral hygiene abstinence: administration of the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), collection of medical history, measurement of hand grip strength, and assessment of a plaque index. This is followed by rinsing with water as a control condition and a subsequent reassessment of th
Assessment of the plaque index after 24 hours of oral hygiene abstinence, followed by mechanical tooth cleaning using a manual toothbrush and subsequent reassessment of the plaque index.
Assessment of the plaque index after 24 hours of oral hygiene abstinence, followed by mechanical tooth cleaning using a U-shaped automatic toothbrush and subsequent reassessment of the plaque index.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Capacity to provide informed consent; sufficient German language proficiency; willingness to attend three study visits (each ≥ 7 days apart)
Exclusion criteria:
Complete dentures; acute periodontitis or acute pain conditions; regular use of U-shaped automatic toothbrushes within the past 2 months; severe hand or arm impairments that make handling a toothbrush impossible; lack of capacity to provide informed consent
